articles.title: Vikings Reportedly Sign Edge Rusher Kyle Van Noy, Reuniting Him With Brian Flores
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have signed edge rusher Kyle Van Noy, reuniting him with defensive coordinator Brian Flores. They won two Super Bowl championships together during their time together with the New England Patriots.
articles.body: With the NFL season about a week away from kickoff, Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley isn’t slowing down constructing the roster. On Tuesday night, the Vikings signed veteran edge rusher Kyle Van Noy, first reported by The Ringer. The 35-year-old veteran reunites with defensive coordinator Brian Flores, with whom he won two Super Bowls on the New England Patriots. Van Noy has bounced around the league over his career. After being drafted in the second round by the Detroit Lions in 2014, he went on to play for the Patriots, the Miami Dolphins under Flores, the Los Angeles Chargers, and most recently, the Baltimore Ravens. ESPN reported early Tuesday morning that Van Noy was visiting Minnesota, and with the visit now wrapped up, the signing is officially done. His 2024 season with the Ravens was highly productive, highlighted by a career-high 12.5 sacks. Van Noy has built a career on leadership and mentorship inside winning organizations, which are qualities head coach Kevin O’Connell could be looking to add in Minnesota. After trading away Pro Bowl edge rusher Jonathan Greenard during the draft, the Vikings were left needing depth and experience upfront. Pairing Van Noy with first-year starter Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel instantly stabilizes their pass-rush rotation. The Vikings also added raw Cincinnati hybrid linebacker Jake Golday in the second round of this year's draft. Adding Van Noy to the fold gives O’Connell and Flores a well-balanced group featuring proven veteran leadership and high-upside depth to start the season. Flores' defense was top-tier last season, ranking third in total yards allowed (282.6) and seventh in points against (19.6). Adding Van Noy as a rotational pass rusher could give the Vikings the extra edge they need for a fast start when they host the Green Bay Packers in Week 1.

articles.title: Cowboys COO Stephen Jones: 'Difficult' To Pay Both CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens
articles.summary: Cowboys COO Stephen Jones expressed pessimism over the team's ability to have both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on long-term deals.
articles.body: Maybe Dallas Cowboys fans should enjoy having CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in the same offense while they still can. "I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market [money], so that's going to be a really difficult situation as we move forward," Cowboys COO Stephen Jones said about Pickens' future in Dallas in an interview on the DLLS Cowboys podcast on Tuesday. "We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year. If everything works out the way we think it is, [in] which CeeDee and George both have huge years again, then it'll be a bigger challenge next year." Coming off a breakout 2025 campaign that saw Pickens total 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns — all three totals led the Cowboys and were career highs — and earn his first career Pro Bowl, Dallas placed the $27.3 million franchise tag on the now-fifth-year receiver in February, whom they acquired from the Pittsburgh Steelers the offseason prior. Meanwhile, the Cowboys signed Lamb, a 2023 All-Pro and a Pro Bowler in each of the last four years, to a four-year, $136 million deal in Aug. 2024. Last season (2025), Lamb totaled 75 receptions for 1,077 yards and three touchdowns across 14 games (he missed three games due to an ankle injury). From 2021-25, Lamb averaged 99.4 receptions for 1,296.2 yards and 7.2 touchdowns per year. Regarding the wide receiver market, Jaxon Smith-Njigba became the highest-paid receiver in NFL history this offseason, inking a four-year, $168.6 million extension ($42.2 million average annual value) with the Seattle Seahawks. On the paying multiple wide receivers top-line money front, the Cincinnati Bengals are paying roughly $69.1 million in salary to Ja'Marr Chase ($40.3 million AAV) and Tee Higgins ($28.8 million AAV), while the Detroit Lions are paying roughly $56.7 million in salary to Amon-Ra St. Brown ($30 million AAV) and Jameson Williams ($26.7 million AAV). Dallas is paying a combined $61.3 million to Lamb and Pickens this season. For perspective, the Bengals haven't made the playoffs since 2022, while the Cowboys haven't reached the playoffs since 2023. "George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another, so it'll help his market," Jones said. "And certainly, I know at some point, as does every player in this league, he'll want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there at wide receiver." Dallas opens its 2026 regular season on the road against the New York Giants on Sept. 13. articles.title: With SEC Expulsion Threats, Could LSU Really Operate As An Independent?
articles.summary: As LSU and the SEC clash, FOX Sports' Ben Portnoy examines the money, power and business decisions reshaping college sports.
articles.body: In Follow The Money, Ben Portnoy will bring you into a weekly deep dive into the business of college sports. Before we jump in, I thought it would be helpful to briefly explain what we’re doing here. College sports have never experienced a more topsy-turvy era. Longtime traditions and the increased need for commercialization are clashing at every turn. Quarterbacks are signing multi-million dollar deals. Television contracts are popular fodder for fan bases. Even jersey patch deals are becoming mainstream. Each week we’ll capture some of the angst and inherent fluidity of the ecosystem as we look at the off-the-field storylines that are shaping what you’re seeing on Saturdays. With that, let’s get into it. The Main Event: SEC, LSU And Potential Independence There is no place quite like Baton Rouge. This is a city where football is king, where politics and the Tigers intertwine like PB&J and where power struggles and backroom dealings are the currency of the day. So what better place to begin the 2026 football season than a Louisiana courtroom? For those who haven’t spent the last two weeks locked into PACER (Public Access to Court Electronic Records) tracking court cases, let’s rehash what’s happening down on the bayou: Yeah, it’s a lot. That said, the LSU situation got me thinking: What if the SEC really did kick the Tigers from the league? And, if it did, what kind of brand value or sponsorship dollars might LSU command on the open market as an independent? "A conference like the SEC is just bigger than a single school," Rob Temple, CEO of Pivotal Sports & Entertainment, told me. "A team moving out of it may have a change or an impact on its sponsors tied to the school or whatever, but the big money around advertising and distribution of content, all that kind of flows to another place. "But the idea of private equity coming into college sports — just like Americans have gone and become owners in the EPL — if that dynamic ever came into college sports, and you got into valuations of franchises, that’s different. That's a huge hypothetical." Independence isn’t anything new in college sports. Notre Dame is the poster child, but others have played this game — BYU in the 2010s and Miami in the 1980s immediately come to mind. Pulling it off these days, however, is increasingly complicated. For one, scheduling is its own challenge. Independent UConn and its administrators have long addressed the issues this poses in trying to piece together a coherent ledger. There’s also a matter of whether LSU would subsequently control its own media rights or whether it'd remain tied to the SEC’s ongoing deal with ESPN. The rights would likely revert to the school, but that’s no guarantee — see Clemson and Florida State’s lawsuits against the ACC in recent years for further proof. Media rights control aside, the most obvious parallel in all of this is Notre Dame, which brings home an annual payout that neighbors the SEC and Big Ten’s media rights distributions in the $75 million range through its NBC deal and arrangement with the ACC. Could LSU fetch that on the open market? That’s less clear. "It's no knock on LSU; it’s just Notre Dame has been Notre Dame, and they've operated independently for so long that to assume LSU would immediately have that same level of independent value is probably unlikely," one media rights consultant told me. "Do they have a good shot of it? Sure, perhaps in the Southwest, but I think the point is, I don't know if they have that same level of national recognition and standing to be considered independent." There’s also the matter of the school’s broader business value. The Athletic conducted a study in July that suggested LSU would be the 11th-most valuable program in the country at around $1.3 billion. That shouldn’t come as a huge surprise. LSU athletics has reported north of $120 million in revenue every year since 2015 and almost $200 million or more since 2022, per the Knight-Newhouse College Athletics Database. It also reported at least $60 million in donor contributions annually since 2022, while corporate sponsorship and licensing dollars have jumped from $3.3 million in 2022 to $5 million in 2025. Pro sports exist in Louisiana, but it’s fall Saturdays at Tiger Stadium that capture the consciousness of the state in a way the Saints and Pelicans can’t quite muster — and why a pending game of chicken between LSU and the SEC has everyone paying attention. "The SEC and Commissioner Sankey are prepared to contest the allegations in the plaintiffs’ petition at Thursday morning’s hearing," the league wrote in a statement released on Sunday night, "and defend the SEC’s rights as a voluntary association to fulfill its mission to its member institutions." Best Quote I Saw This Week "This whole thing is ridiculous. Don’t hate the player, hate the game." — Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry in a statement to Front Office Sports on the ongoing eligibility fight in the state. Best Deal I Saw This Week Duke announced a five-year agreement with Edward Jones, which, at face-value, isn’t going to force eyebrows to raise. That the Blue Devils brass is allowing the company to place its branding on the floor at Cameron Indoor Stadium, however, is noteworthy. "It’s balancing our needs with the history and tradition, evolving with the current landscape and figuring out what is right to do here," Duke athletics director Nina King told me by phone. "I'm just really excited by how this looks. It's not like, ‘Oh my goodness, we turned into NASCAR.’" Michigan added signage within the Big House for the first time in recent weeks. Now, Duke is following suit. Such is life in college sports these days. articles.title: Lions GM Brad Holmes explains cutting Greg Dortch
articles.summary: "When you add as much competition as possible... it adds more discomfort, (and) it also entails harder decisions," Detroit Lions GM Brad Holmes said.
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK — The Detroit Lions ' decision to release Greg Dortch left many puzzled, including the receiver himself .

Asked why the Lions moved on from Dortch, who looked like he was on track to be Detroit's No. 4 option at receiver and the team's best punt returner, Lions general manager Brad Holmes said it was simply a matter of competition, and Dortch found himself on the outside looking in.

"We wanted to add as much competition as possible this whole offseason. Look, when you add as much competition as possible — it was fierce competition — it adds more discomfort, (and) it also entails harder decisions," Holmes said Wednesday, Sept. 2.. "That's really all it was. (Dortch) was just part of that competition, and unfortunately it just didn't work out. So, that's why we made the move we made."

The Lions ultimately kept four receivers on their initial 53-man roster (Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Tay Martin) and brought three more back to their practice squad, in Tom Kennedy, Lucky Jackson and Dominic Lovett. Teams can temporarily elevate players from the practice squad for three games in a single season, which the Lions could do early in the season, with Kennedy being the most obvious candidate.

"Four (receivers) is obviously a little bit on the lighter side. That's just where we're at right now, today, currently," Holmes said. "But I do like the different flavors in that room. Obviously, we all know St. Brown and Jamo and TeSlaa. I know (TeSlaa) dropped a couple balls in a preseason game, but I thought he a had a good camp, too. Just the little things that he does in the run, which, those aren't little things, those are actually really big things that he does in the run game. I thought that he improved with his route running, his releases, all those things."

Martin, 28, signed with the Lions in June after standing out with the UFL's Columbus Aviators. Undrafted in 2022, Martin has made NFL stops with the San Francisco 49ers (2022-24), Tennessee Titans (2024) and Washington Commanders (2025).

Lions coach Dan Campbell praised Martin multiple times throughout training camp, including Aug. 11, when Campbell said Martin "makes plays ever day." Martin has three career catches for 72 yards and a touchdown. He's also played 70 snaps on special teams, including 33 on kickoff coverage and 26 on kickoff return.

In this year's preseason, Martin caught six of his 10 targets for 41 yards and a score.

"He made it relatively easy throughout camp, in terms of his contributions in the run game, his contributions on special teams, and he showed the ability to win one on ones," Holmes said of Martin. "When you're doing all those components at that position, especially when you're looking at towards the back end, you can fit in right here."

articles.title: Everything Florida football coach Jon Sumrall said on his first SEC teleconference
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall discusses Florida's opener, QB room and more on SEC media call. Here's everything he had to say.
articles.body:
Florida football coach Jon Sumrall made his debut on the SEC's media teleconference call on Wednesday, Sept. 2.

This week's call will be one of five this season, which includes 10 minutes of questions for each of the conference's head coaches.

First-year coach Jon Sumrall will make his debut leading Florida against Florida Atlantic on Saturday, Sept. 5, with kickoff set for 7:45 p.m. at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. The game will be televised on the SEC Network.

Here's what Sumrall had to say on this week's media call.

"Yeah, our team, we had practice this morning. We play Saturday at 7:55 (sic) against FAU, and we're excited about it."

QUESTION: What are some non-negotiables for Florida in his first game as head coach?

Sumrall: "You got to play with enthusiasm and passion, effort, and you wanna see them strain. You only get 12 regular-season opportunities, and you don't want to take any of them for granted, ever. And I'd like for us to play like we've practiced, you know? Look like we've done some things before and operate efficiently. You see so many common mistakes that happen in Week 1 or Week 0 games like last week, and just for us to do what we've prepared in a crisp, clean manner is sort of the way you want to see it happen. But there will be guys making mistakes; when they do, I want to see them make them full speed. I want to see them go as hard as they can from the snap through the echo of the whistle."

QUESTION: How has the offensive line shown growth throughout the offseason, and where (offensive line coach) Phil Trautwein has shined ?

Sumrall: "Yeah, Phil is really detailed. He's a great teacher. He's very consistent. Phil's a guy who doesn't get too high or too low; he shows up the same way every day. Like I said, consistency is a key there, I think. And I think just finding ways to help guys maximize who they are. Different guys receive things in different ways from a coaching standpoint, and so, how we reach each player is a little bit unique. But he's very thorough with his preparation for his guys, and I think he's done a great job. I did not shy away from -- when we got here, I felt that the offensive line was an area that needed massive improvement. I think we've made improvement. Is it high enough for us to play the game at a level that we desire to? We're gonna find out real soon."

QUESTION: How will you feel when you run out of the tunnel ?

Sumrall: "I'm going to be pretty excited about it. I've said this a lot: I think back to when I was on the opposite sideline a couple times here as a player and as a coach, and how unique and special I've always felt like The Swamp is. And the fanbase here is so electric and charged up that I'll be very similarly wired. That gameday opportunity here is unlike many out there. And so, I'll be amped up. But at the end of the day too, it's really about focusing on us doing our job to the best of our ability and playing really good football. And so you have to make sure that while you're emotionally charged up and you're hyped, that you don't forget that the main things that go on within the game aren't in the stands; it's in between the white lines, and how do we help put our guys in situations to be successful."

QUESTION: What is the appreciation level of being an SEC head coach after growing up in the South ?

Sumrall: "I appreciate the shout out to Ronny Massey. What a great man. You know, I feel appreciation every day I walk into our building. We've got the Gator head logo above our main entrance, and every time I walk in our building, I get excited about being here. And I don't take any day at the office for granted. But, you know, to your point, growing up, I really idolized SEC football. I would watch every SEC game that was on TV or listen to a bunch of them on the radio as a kid, and to be able to have the privilege of leading an SEC team as a head coach is something I've dreamed about my entire coaching career. And, for me, it's the opportunity of a lifetime, and I will never take it for granted, and will always have great appreciation for the situation I'm in."

QUESTION: On how much more competitive the QB room has been from spring to fall?

Sumrall: "That's a great question. I'd say, if you asked me in early April who was going to start for us, it really wasn't much of a conversation, because of the difference in how well Philo operated at the line of scrimmage and ran the offense. The beautiful thing is Philo's continued to grow and get better, but so has the room. Tramell has stepped up and made strides. Aidan Warner has been really consistent and steady when he's had opportunities present. Will Griffin is uber talented, the freshman we got from Tampa. And then Aaron Williams is also in that room, does a great job adding value to our football team. But the whole room is elevated, which has made it more competitive, which is good for everybody. You know, you don't want anybody to become the starter because there's not great depth in the room. You want one guy just to elevate a little bit above the others, and I've got a lot of confidence in everybody in that quarterback room, though, that when they have opportunities, they're going to be ready to go."

Florida football offers final preseason glimpse before Sept. 5 opener

QUESTION: A theme from you has been urgency for this team. You have to get to the game before you realize that, but is it where you want it to go into the season?

Sumrall: "I think it is, but you never know until you play. I think in preparation our urgency has improved. I think what you find out on Saturday is what your level of detail and doing your job at an elite level against another team, and it's not maybe in a practice environment against maybe people you play against every day. There's going to be some adversity hit in every game at every point all year. That's the biggest thing you can't really fully prepare for. We simulate a lot of things to try and create what that looks like around our building and practices all the time. But there's nothing like it happening in a live game. We'll see what our urgency looks like against another opponent here shortly. I look forward to seeing how we respond to a lot of different situations that come up within games."

QUESTION: From a special teams standpoint, not just kicking field goals, but overall how would you assess your special teams heading into Game 1?

Sumrall: "We've got Patrick Durkin as our starting field goal kicker. He was 25 of 28 last year and had a handful of them, I think four over 50 yards. So he's steady. He's got real ability. Yesterday on kickoffs, he was hitting most of them, eight, nine deep in the end zone, so he's got high touchback capability. Alec Clark is our punter who's been starting punter in college football now for a couple of years. He's really efficient, catch-to-kick. He's usually fast getting the ball off and really is a consistent punter in regard to distance and hang. I like how he does things. The other thing that Alec does at an elite level is he handles the short snaps really well on field goal and extra points. He's as good of a holder as I've ever been around, which probably doesn't get talked about enough. Snapping-wise, Carter Milliron will handle our long snaps on punt. He's played a lot of college football as a fifth-year senior. Then Lincoln Anderson is going to handle our short snaps, who is a true freshman from Hoover, Alabama, but has done a really good job this entire training camp and really shown that he is ready for this moment. Look forward to watching him perform, so those are our main specialists that will start and go on Saturday."

QUESTION: What were your first impressions of Jayden Woods? How far do you think he can go in his career?

Sumrall: "My first impression was positive, and it's only become more positive after that. He's a guy; when we got here, he was a high priority for us to retain. Then he made the decision to enter the transfer portal to just test the waters and see what was out there. We were able to hold on and get him to stay at the University of Florida, and I was pretty excited when that happened. I'm even more excited about the fact that he made the decision to stay each and every day that I get to work with him. He's really, really talented. But more so than just being talented, he's as good of a human you could ever want to be around. He works at a really high level. He's very detailed. He's got great pride in his craft, and he's a high-character guy. I think the sky is the limit for what Jayden can achieve on the field. But what makes it fun working with him day in, day out is just holistically he's a fantastic person. He has high standards for himself in every area of his life and not just football. He's going to be successful in any endeavor he takes on just because of the way he's wired. So very grateful he's on our football team. Like I said, I was excited off my first impression that we got to keep him. I'm even more excited now."

articles.title: NBA champion gives respect to young Sixers guard VJ Edgecombe
articles.summary: NBA champion Jason Williams gives his respect to young Philadelphia 76ers guard VJ Edgecombe heading into his second season.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers guard VJ Edgecombe is set to enter his second season in the league looking to continue to establish himself as a rising star in this league. The No. 3 pick of the 2025 draft was impressive as a rookie with averages of 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 4.2 assists along with coming up big in big moments countless times.

Edgecombe was fantastic throughout his maiden NBA season, and now will be able to learn from the likes of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in his second. The explosive guard out of Baylor might not be one of the top options anymore, but the Sixers could do much worse than having Edgecombe as their No. 5 option on this roster when considering the talent around him.

2006 NBA champion Jason Williams is impressed with Edgecombe as he stated:

The best 5 option ever on earth. Maybe. Name one better? Edgecombe's the 5th option, bro. Come on.

They then began thinking of previous No. 5 options and thought about the old Miami Heat teams and the old Golden State Warriors teams. Williams continued:

I'll probably take Edgecombe over my man (Shane) Battier...I'm still going Edgecombe over DeMarcus Cousins, bro.

One has to wonder about Edgecombe's development when considering his bump down in the offensive hierarchy, but he can do so many different things on the floor that will impact winning and that allows him to be helpful for this group no matter what is going on. The Sixers will find a way to prioritize his development in certain moments to help him continue to grow.

articles.title: Alex Afari receives TRO to potentially play for Kentucky in 2026
articles.summary: In a summer filled with court cases, Kentucky may add a fifth year linebacker in Alex Afari after he received TRO protection following a court ruling.
articles.body:
Kentucky football received a massive addition to the roster today. After a summer full of court cases, Kentucky's Alex Afari entered the fold to try and get a fifth year of eligibility. Louisville Circuit Court Judge Brian Edwards ruled in favor of Afari, allowing him to join the lawsuit against the NCAA, which gives Afari a temporary restraining order (TRO) to return to the Wildcats and play a fifth season of college football. Afari practiced with the team in August, until the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals briefly ruled him ineligible.

All of this court case talk goes over a lot of our heads, me included, and it is just constantly moving which makes it extremely difficult to keep track. Afari is an interesting case specifically, as mentioned in his court case, Afari did not sign an NFL contract. Afari had a medical waiver to participate in a tryout with the Green Bay Packers. According to the SEC, the criteria they set for the class of 2022 athletes to return to the field for a fifth year lines up to a tee with Afari's case.

Now, the addition of Afari would help out Jay Bateman's defense a ton. Afari has suited up in 48 games over his four years with the Wildcats, the safety-turned-linebacker tallied 193 tackles, 26.5 tackles for loss, six sacks and forced a fumble over that span. He will add to a linebacker room that is in need of depth and experience. Grant Godfrey is expected to take a step after last season, outside of Godfrey, the Wildcats have a group of talented but inexperienced backers in Elijah Barnes, Tavion Wallace and Antwan Smith. The Wildcats now have five linebackers that will be in the rotation this fall.

Overall, the addition of Afari could flip this position group from being an unknown into a strength. The defensive staff should feel confident in this unit to go out and exceed expectations in 2026. Afari brings a veteran presence as someone who has played a ton of SEC football over the last four seasons. The Wildcats will be able to showcase the new defensive scheme on Saturday against Youngstown State at 1 P.M. ET at Kroger Field.

Will Stein commented on this news during the SEC teleconference. "There are still some things that have to happen, I think, for us to feel really confident about playing him." said Stein. This a promising step in the right direction for Afari to get on the field this fall.

articles.title: Title-chasing Somerset punish Glamorgan on day one
articles.summary: Somerset dominate Glamorgan on day one of their Division One match to boost their title chase.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, The Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton (day one)

Glamorgan 194: Kellaway 51; Pretorius 3-45

Somerset's slip fielders shared seven catches as Glamorgan were bowled out for 194 on a one-sided opening day of the Rothesay County Championship First Division match at Taunton.

Henry Nicholls and Tom Abell claimed three each and Craig Overton one as all the Welsh county's wickets fell to catches behind the stumps. Wicketkeeper James Rew also pouched three to reward seamers Migael Pretorius (3-45), Lewis Gregory (2-58), Overton (2-63) and Tom Lammonby (2-27).

Ben Kellaway top-scored with 51 after Glamorgan had been invited to bat first in overcast conditions on a green-tinged pitch offering good carry and just sufficient seam movement for the pace bowlers, who also benefited from some swing.

By the close, Somerset had replied with 92-0 on a day which suggested they are well capable of clinching a first ever Championship title in what is building towards a thrilling finale to the red ball season.

Josh Thomas was unbeaten on 46 and Tom Lammonby 37 not out, having batted with an assurance that, Kellaway apart, was absent from the Glamorgan innings.

The visitors looked to be making a good fist of things after the start of play had been delayed for half an hour by rain. Mason Crane and Asa Tribe took the score to 33 in the eighth over before the latter edged Pretorius through to Rew, who took an excellent low catch diving to his right.

It was 45-2 when Kiran Carlson presented a waist-high catch to first slip Nicholls off Pretorius and 49-3 when second slip Abell accepted a chance offered by Crane on 27, with Overton the successful bowler.

A brief shower interrupted play at 68-3, but when the action resumed there was still time before lunch for Colin Ingram to edge Gregory to Abell and leave Glamorgan 80-4 going into the afternoon session.

Kellaway produced some sweetly-timed drives to move to a half-century off 81 balls. But the following delivery from Pretorius saw him edge to Nicholls and soon it was 125-6 as former Somerset player Sean Dickson, celebrating his 35th birthday, was snared in the slips by Overton driving at a wide ball from Gregory.

Further edges brought the downfalls of Chris Cooke, Dan Douthwaite and Connor O'Riordan before Timm van der Gugten pulled a defiant six off Pretorius and shared a last-wicket stand of 36 with Mir Hamza, who was last man out to Jack Leach - the only wicket to fall to spin.

Tea was taken immediately, but further rain delayed a restart, with nine overs added to the four lost in the morning session.

Conditions remained bowler-friendly, with the floodlights on, for the beginning of Somerset's reply. But, after a watchful start, openers Thomas and Lammonby soon increased the tempo, Thomas smiting three successive fours off Hamza in the sixth over.

The two left-handers brought up a half-century stand in 11.1 overs, looking in total control. Lammonby, on 19, edged van der Gugten just short of first slip, but it was a rare moment of anxiety as Glamorgan's bowlers struggled to match the home attack's penetration.

As the sun broke through for the first time, batting looked easier than it had done all day. By stumps, Thomas and Lammonby had shared 12 boundaries and put their side in an immensely strong position on a day when title rivals were inhibited by the weather.

articles.title: Equestrian: Russian athletes cleared to compete at FEI events
articles.summary: The International Equestrian Federation lifts its ban on Russian athletes and officials after four and a half years.
articles.body:
The International Equestrian Federation has lifted its ban on Russian athletes and officials after four and a half years.

Riders, horses and officials from Russia and Belarus have been prohibited from representing their countries under their national flags at FEI events since March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

The international governing body will also allow events to be held in Russia as part of regulations that will come into effect on 5 October.

The move means participants from Russia and Belarus will no longer be required to compete as Neutral Individual Athletes.

The FEI's decision comes after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced in June that it would provisionally lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee.

It means athletes from the region could potentially be cleared to represent Russia at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

Following its announcement, the FEI said it would like to "take this opportunity to reiterate its support for the people of Ukraine".

articles.title: After NHL Trade Rumors, Robert Thomas Named 25th Captain in Blues History
articles.summary: St. Louis Blues center Robert Thomas has gone from rumored trade candidate to team captain.
articles.body:
St. Louis Blues center Robert Thomas has gone from rumored trade candidate to team captain.

Thomas has been named the 25th captain in Blues franchise history, the team announced Wednesday.

Colton Parayko, Philip Broberg, Jake Neighbours and Dylan Holloway will serve as assistant captains, according to the Blues.

Lawyer for Hospitalized ASU Hockey Player Wants Answers

Thomas was subject to trade rumors ahead of the midseason trade deadline last March. The Minnesota Wild made an offer for him that was declined by the Blues, according to The Athletic's Michael Russo .

Those trade talks were in part because Thomas is signed through the 2030-31 season at an $8.125 million AAV, a relative bargain for a first-line center in a market that has ballooned in an offseason capped off by Macklin Celebrini's record $18.8 million AAV deal.

Thomas told The Athletic's Jeremy Rutherford in July the Blues had never asked him to waive his no-trade clause.

He also told Rutherford he was involved with meetings this offseason with front office members including new general manager Alexander Steen about the direction of the team.

Thomas at the time named Holloway, Neighbours and Broberg as three players who made him hopeful for the Blues' future.

That trio will now take on leadership roles alongside two veteran Blues players in Parayko, who is heading into his 12th season in St. Louis, and Thomas, who is the seventh Blues draft pick in franchise history to captain the franchise.

Selected with the No. 20 pick of the 2017 NHL draft, Thomas made his NHL debut the following year and appeared in 21 playoff games during the Blues' run to the 2019 Stanley Cup.

He has produced at a point-per-game rate in three of the last four years, including when he recorded 64 points (25 games, 39 assists) in 64 games while shooting an NHL-best 24.5 percent last season.

Despite missing time during the 2025-26 campaign after undergoing a midseason leg procedure, Thomas was the most productive player on a roster that ultimately missed the postseason for the third time in four years.

Thomas will hope his and Parayko's leadership combined with the Blues' new and younger core will help improve this team's chances of winning a playoff round for the first time since 2022.

articles.title: Joel Klatt's 10 Burning Questions Going Into The 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: FOX Sports lead college football analyst Joel Klatt answers 10 burning questions heading into Week 1, including which teams can actually win it all.
articles.body: Who runs college football? Can Indiana repeat as national champions? Which team is ready to make the leap? And is LSU officially college football's new villain? The 2026 college football season is here, and the biggest questions in the sport are waiting to be answered. FOX Sports lead college football analyst Joel Klatt has plenty of thoughts. On the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show," Klatt tackles 10 burning questions heading into Week 1, including which teams can actually win it all. Will The Big Ten Continue Its Run Over The SEC? Klatt's Thoughts: "I think this is the biggest question in college football. … The last three National Championships have come out of the Big Ten: Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana. But it's been even more than that because, for so long, the SEC dominated. They were the premier conference in college football by a wide margin. They won everything. … It was also that way in the NFL Draft, every single year, it was the SEC with the most players drafted in the first round … Over the last few years, we've seen the shift happen, not just at the top winning the championships, but also in the records in these bowl games, and, last year, in the first round of the NFL Draft. "In the last three seasons, the SEC is 0-4 against the Big Ten in the College Football Playoff. … Every single metric you used to hear about and, candidally, the ones that matter, these games that matter, the first-round draft picks, the elite talent, the Big Ten has overtaken the SEC. … I predict that the Big Ten is going to win another championship this year." Is Indiana Going To Be Good Again? Klatt's Thoughts: "This is an emphatic ‘Yes.’ Indiana is a powerhouse right now. Curt Cignetti, I think, is the best coach in college football. That was proven last year. That roster was not as expensive as all the rosters that they were beating in the College Football Playoff. … Cignetti retained all of his staff. This is the one thing that I think is going to be hard to wrap your minds around. They were 16-0 and national champions last year, and the conversations that I'm having with people around the program at Indiana is that they're quietly ahead of where they were each of the last two years right now with this team. There is a chance this is a better team. … "Josh Hoover is further along in the offense and with his comfort in the offense than Fernando Mendoza was last year or Kurtis Rourke was two years ago. That's something that they point to. The offensive line is further along. … Their front seven on defense might be better than last year, and this was one of the best defenses in college football." Who’s Going To Be The Face Of College Football? Klatt's Thoughts: "I think the quarterback class is outstanding. You've got Dante Moore, Arch Manning, CJ Carr, Julian Sayin, Darian Mensah, Jayden Maiava, Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It is littered with guys who could potentially become that guy in college football … Oh, by the way, I haven't even mentioned the guy who is widely considered the best skill position player we've seen in college football, maybe in our lifetimes, but certainly in over a decade in Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The potential is limitless for college football this year. "It could be an unbelievable year, and the guy that grabs the sport and brings it down and becomes the face of the sport is going to be the one that plays the best in high-leverage moments and on big stages. That's what it becomes, and that guy's ultimately going to be the Heisman Trophy winner. … My pick to win the Heisman Trophy is Jeremiah Smith." Will Arch Manning, Steve Sarkisian & Texas Finally Raise Their Ceiling? Klatt's Thoughts: "I think that [new defensive coordinator] Will Muschamp is going to have a huge impact on this season because if he fixes that defense, then, yes, Arch, Sark and Texas can raise their ceiling, but that's really where it lies. It's not with Arch and Sark. It's with Will Muschamp, the offensive line and the defense. Those are the areas for Texas that have got to change. Obviously, they have a difficult schedule. They've got that Ohio State game. They've got to play at Tennessee. They've got Red River [Oklahoma]. They've got Ole Miss. They've got three road trips in November: Missouri, LSU and Texas A&M. "So this schedule is daunting. There's no doubt, but they are one of the more talented teams in the country. And if they run it and play good defense, then they could easily win a national championship." Which New Coaches Are Going To Make A Huge Impact In Year 1? Klatt's Thoughts: "Eric Morris at Oklahoma State. He goes from North Texas to Oklahoma State and takes a bunch of his guys with him. Does it remind you of anybody? Yeah, this is exactly what Curt Cignetti did when he went from James Madison to Indiana, and they popped right away and went to the College Football Playoff. Bob Chesney, now going from James Madison to UCLA. Now, I think it will be much more difficult for UCLA than it would be for Oklahoma State because I think the Big Ten is more difficult than the Big 12, but this is a guy who has a quarterback in Nico Iamaleava, and they can increase their win total drastically right away. This is a really good coach. "I also feel the same way about James Franklin at Virginia Tech. James is a hell of a football coach. At Penn State, his only problem was that he couldn't get all the way to the mountaintop, but, man, he's a great climber. He built a really solid program at Penn State. He did a great job there, couldn't get to the mountaintop, and now he's at Virginia Tech, and I think he will immediately make them better. Those are guys I think could elevate their programs right away." Who Can Actually Win The National Championship? Klatt's Thoughts: "I've got seven teams that can absolutely win a national championship this year. They've got the roster and everything that you need. … Oregon, Notre Dame, Ohio State, Georgia, Indiana, Texas, Miami: I won't be surprised at all if any of them win the national championship. It's what makes the sport great this year, by the way. I think that's a deeper, more eclectic list than we've had maybe ever in college football, but easily in multiple decades." Are Lane Kiffin And LSU The New Villain In The Sport? Klatt's Thoughts: "They're absolutely the villain. … Now, you have the SEC actively against LSU and Lane Kiffin [the Tigers have been trying to add players who appeared on NFL rosters in training camp to their roster]. … There's no doubt in my mind that he's the villain in college football … "It would be the shock of all shocks to me if they came together from a chemistry perspective to run the table, win the SEC and win the national championship. It is a different equation now. I think it takes more than talent and a great offensive mind to go and win a national championship. It takes everything. You've got to have chemistry, depth, experience and togetherness. All these things are really hard to build. That's what it takes. Do they have that? I don't know." Which Teams Will Level Up In Each Conference? Klatt's Thoughts: "Maybe it's BYU out of the Big 12? In the Big Ten, I look at USC, Michigan, Penn State and Washington trying to level themselves up. These teams are very good teams, but you got to prove to me that you can potentially beat one of the top dogs. In the SEC, you got Alabama, LSU, Texas A&M, Oklahoma, and all these different teams. My money would be on three teams that I think have the talent, coaching and potential to actually go up there and beat one of these top-tier teams in these conferences. In the Big Ten, that's USC and Michigan, and in the SEC, it would be LSU, just because of that talent, but we'll see about the chemistry." Who Could Be This Year’s Indiana? (Dark Horse) Klatt's Thoughts: "How about Texas Tech and Ole Miss taking the next step? … I would not have told you at this point last year that Indiana had the roster or the chemistry or the experience or any of that to go win a national championship, and they did. Maybe that's the case for Texas Tech? They beat up on teams that they should and lost to the best team that they faced in Oregon last year. Everyone's overlooking Ole Miss because Lane Kiffin left. What if they galvanize around Pete Golding with their great quarterback, Trinidad Chambliss, and they move forward and win the SEC? Maybe they just run roughshod over college football, and they become this year's 2025 Indiana." Is The Sport Better Than Ever? Klatt's Thoughts: "It's absolutely ‘Yes.’ For all the things that aren't perfect in this sport, all of these changes, however hard they have been to swallow, to watch and work through, have made the sport better. There's been more engagement than ever with college football. … "Whatever you think about NIL and whatever you think about the transfer portal and whatever you think about the mess that is college football right now from a governance standpoint, these changes, however hard to swallow, have made the sport incredible. We've got great teams. We've got talent all over the country, and we have every single part of this country represented with high expectations and expectations all the way at the top, as high as winning the national championship. That makes it great. We've got great quarterbacks and players. This could be an epic season of college football."

articles.title: DFB-Pokal: Bayern overcome early Osnabrück scare to reach second round
articles.summary: Despite Robin Meißner giving the hosts a dream start with a spectacular goal, Bayern’s class and experience eventually shone through. Goals from Harry Kane a...
articles.body:
Despite Robin Meißner giving the hosts a dream start with a spectacular goal, Bayern's class and experience eventually shone through. Goals from Harry Kane and Tom Bischof turned the game around before second-half strikes from Michael Olise and Kane's penalty completed a 4-1 victory for Vincent Kompany's men.

It was Osnabrück who made the perfect start, stunning the holders after just five minutes. Bayern failed to deal with a long ball, which eventually fell to Meißner. The forward brought it down before unleashing a spectacular volley from distance that flew past the helpless Jonas Urbig to make it 1-0.

Their lead lasted just 13 minutes, however, before Bayern hit back. Robin Fabinski's attempted clearance went up rather than out and fell straight into the path of Kane, who calmly tucked the ball home from inside the area to level proceedings. The goal also extended Kane's remarkable run of scoring in seven consecutive DFB-Pokal appearances.

Six minutes later, Bayern had completed the comeback. Olise slipped the ball through to Luis Díaz, whose effort was saved by Jonas Krumrey. However, the rebound fell kindly to Bischof, who made no mistake from close range, sliding the ball into the far corner to give Bayern their first lead of the evening.

Bayern continued to control proceedings and almost extended their advantage deep into first-half stoppage time when Olise found space on the edge of the area. His curling effort looked destined for the corner, but Krumrey produced an excellent save to keep Osnabrück within one goal at the break.

The second half was quieter in terms of quality and clear-cut chances, though Bayern continued to manage the game comfortably and offered Osnabrück little hope of mounting a comeback. The hosts failed to register another shot on target in the second half, with their last effort on target having come in the 21st minute.

Bayern finally added the goal that put the result beyond doubt in the 73rd minute, with Olise finding the net. The visitors won possession high up the pitch through substitute Lennart Karl, who then fed the Frenchman inside the area. Olise skipped past a challenge from Fabinski before calmly slotting the ball past Krumrey to make it 3-1.

Kompany's men added further gloss to the scoreline four minutes from time when Aleksandar Pavlović was brought down by Jannik Müller inside the area, resulting in a penalty. Kane stepped up and sent Krumrey the wrong way to make it 4-1.

The cup holders saw out the remaining minutes, including added time, with little difficulty to secure a comfortable victory and their place in the second round of the DFB-Pokal.

articles.title: For the birds: Medvedev protests US Open umpire's call to replay a point after birds sit on the net
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev thought the chair umpire's call was for the birds.  Medvedev protested a decision Wednesday during his second-round victory at the U.S. Open...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Daniil Medvedev thought the chair umpire's call was for the birds.

Medvedev protested a decision Wednesday during his second-round victory at the U.S. Open after the umpire ordered a point to be replayed because two birds sat on top of the net during multiple shots of a rally.

Medvedev led 4-1 in the second set with Sebastian Gorzny serving. Two small birds sat atop the net in Louis Armstrong Stadium during the middle of a point and play continued, with both players hitting multiple shots before Medvedev angled a forehand toward the corner that caused one of the birds to fly up. Umpire Timo Janzen quickly signaled for play to stop as Gorzny began to hit a shot that would not have gotten back into play.

"This is the most ridiculous decisions I've seen in my life," Medvedev said. "This is very bad."

Medvedev, no stranger to chaotic moments in Armstrong, was asked following his 6-1, 6-3, 7-5 victory where that one ranked.

"This would be definitely in the top five," he said. "But the thing is that when they came in, I thought, OK, the referee is going to stop the point, and he let it play, like, 'OK, let's play.' And the moment I hit the winner, he was, like, 'Stop! Stop! Stop!'"

Medvedev lost his first-round match in Armstrong last year, when his meltdown after the umpire allowed Benjamin Bonzi a second serve because a photographer mistakenly entered the court too soon led to a delay of more than six minutes. His antics on the same court in 2019, followed by a postmatch interview in which he encouraged fans to continue raining down boos on him, led to a $9,000 fine.

He quickly let go of Wednesday's incident.

"It's OK," the 2021 champion said. "It happens."

articles.title: 76ers' Tacko Fall gives fiery message after teaming up with ex-teammate Jaylen Brown, LeBron James

articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have assembled quite the squad for the next couple of seasons after having one of the best offseasons in the entire league. There was not much of a shot at landing LeBron James initially, but that changed after Philadelphia traded for Jaylen Brown.

The 76ers then added Kentavious Caldwell-Pope after acquiring those two NBA champions. With the moves Philadelphia has made, the team has the potential to make a deep playoff run and compete for a championship.

"You've got to acknowledge Philly's potential this season with the addition of James and Jaylen Brown, even if Embiid is not a good bet to play more than half the year or be in good form when the playoffs roll around. Brown, James and Tyrese Maxey will keep the Sixers highly relevant, but it'll probably take a miraculous turning back of the clock from Embiid to reach contender status," Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes wrote.

Philadelphia is still looking for smaller ways to improve the roster. On Tuesday, the 76ers signed Tacko Fall to an Exhibit 10 contract.

"The Philadelphia 76ers have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr. and Saint Thomas, the team announced. All three players are on Exhibit 10 deals, a source told ESPN, and will be a part of Sixers training camp," ESPN's Dave McMenamin posted.

This is an incredible opportunity for Fall to potentially work his way toward a two-way contract, which could allow him to compete for a spot in the NBA. He also delivered a strong message about potentially teaming up with Jaylen Brown again and playing alongside LeBron James for the first time.

"It is an opportunity of a lifetime that I shall not waste," Fall said.

Any team could use a 7-foot-6 player on its roster, but it ultimately comes down to whether Fall can prove that he deserves the opportunity. Fall has appeared in the NBA before, but he has yet to establish himself with a team for an extended period.

With Fall now getting an opportunity to compete for a team with legitimate championship aspirations, he could have more motivation than ever. The 7-foot-6 center knows there is a lot at stake for his NBA career, and he will have to do whatever it takes to prove he belongs in Philadelphia.

articles.title: John Harbaugh, Greg Newsome II weigh in on Giants cornerback competition
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh and defensive back Greg Newsome II speak to the media about the team's position battle at cornerback with under two...
articles.body:
The Giants 53-man roster having just been released , many are wondering which cornerbacks will get the starting nod from new head coach John Harbaugh when they take the field at MetLife Stadium on the night of Sunday, Sep. 13.

Right now, it appears that Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II have the upper hand on the two starting boundary cornerback spots in the aggressive 3-4 scheme set to be deployed under new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson .

Harbaugh was asked on Wednesday if he feels "secure" about Newsome's potential role as a starter.

"We do," Harbaugh responded. "He has been very, very consistent every day... we expect him to play at a high level."

Harbaugh's response to a question asking where the competition for gameday snaps stands at the cornerback position?

"It stands where it stands. We'll be moving forward with it, and see where it goes... it could be a rotation, or it could be two guys out there the whole game."

The other cornerbacks vying for playing time are Dru Phillips , Paulson Adebo , Nic Jones , and 2026 second-round draft selection Colton Hood .

Despite his unofficial designation as a starter, Newsome himself had nothing but praise to offer his position-mates.

"I think we have the best cornerback room in the league when you talk about depth and guys who have the ability to play," Newsome asserted.

"Tae [Banks] has been amazing, his press coverage is very strong and very physical... Hood, being a rookie, he takes a lot from us vets, he asks questions, he learns, he's been growing each and every day... I think everyone has been doing a great job."

Of course, with Newsome expected to cover Ceedee Lamb and George Pickens - two of the best wide receivers in the NFL - in Week 1, he made sure to take the time to hype himself up as well.

"I'm super excited for the challenge, and I'll be ready," Newsome proclaimed.

"I believe I am a starter in this league, I believe I'm a top corner in this league," he concluded. "Now it's time to prove it every single day."

articles.title: Four Observations from Bayern Munich’s 4-1 win over VfL Osnabrück
articles.summary: Bayern Munich managed a comeback in the DFB Pokal.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich headed to Osnabrück to rewrite the iconic defeat where Bayern fell short in a massive upset in 1978. While many things have changed since then, the Bavarians remained massive favorites heading into this match. Luckily, this time Bayern ended on the right side of history.

VfL Osnabrück caught Bayern early by surprise, but it wasn't a reason to panic

The home side opened the game in quite an odd fashion, resulting in a special moment for the fans, giving them the idea that the unthinkable could happen. Based on Bayern's recent exits in the DFB Pokal, it also gave the away fans a moment of horror. However, as unfortunate of a fluke it was by Jonathan Tah to miss the clearance, and for Jonas Urbig to be caught off guard with the long-shot, Robin Meißner simply scored a stunning goal, one that will get past the best from time to time. It was not a moment to panic, and Vincent Kompany's side did a great job of staying calm and on plan.

Tom Bischof's shooting ability is one of the best in football

You heard that right. Tom Bischof has one of the best striking abilities in the world at the moment. He can shoot from range, he can shoot from mid-distance, and he can also hit a precise finish from close as well. The kind of calmness he has with his strikes shows experience far beyond his years, and while Kompany shouldn't rush him to start at striker, he is an incredibly versatile option in midfield.

Did Jonas Urbig have a bad game? Not necessarily. But the facts are that Urbig is getting fewer opportunities than he deserves at the moment, and with that in mind, it feels like he has to prove himself every game. Unfortunately, he was caught massively off guard for the opening goal and never really had the chance to prove himself later in the match. Urbig is still destined for big things, but he will have that goal running in his mind for a while.

Michael Olisé will go down as one of the best footballers of the generation

Watching Olisé play is a truly special gift. There are simply very few players to ever play that are as talented as the Frenchman. This isn't exactly a new observation, but sometimes you just have to re-state the obvious. There is no one in the world that can doubt his talent, and Bayern Munich need to give a massive raise to the scouts that convinced the club to sign him from Crystal Palace. Convincing him to stay long-term is another issue, but hopefully an issue that the club doesn't have to worry about for a long time. For now, enjoy one of the most talented players ever.

articles.title: Will the Kawhi Leonard Clippers-Raptors trade go ahead with NBA investigation ending?
articles.summary: The trade was put on hold pending the NBA's investigation.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers agreed to trade star forward Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors back on June 30. But Leonard's reunion with the Raptors was effectively put on hold pending the NBA's investigation into the Clippers' impermissible endorsements for Leonard.

The Raptors basically wanted to make sure that they were trading for a player who was actually going to be able to play. And on Wednesday, the Raptors got their answer.

The NBA announced a series of sanctions against the Clippers, owner Steve Ballmer and team execs Gillian Zucker and Lawrence Frank. And while Leonard was punished after the investigation concluded, his discipline was significantly lighter than what Ballmer and company faced.

According to the NBA's statement , Leonard would be required to pay a $700,000 fine for his part in circumventing the salary cap. He was not suspended.

Given that Leonard's playing status wasn't impacted in the penalties, it sounds like the deal will go through. Leonard released a statement that mentioned his return to Toronto.

The trade — which sent Leonard to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, 2030 and 2033 second-round picks and a 2027 first-round pick swap — should happen.

articles.title: Orioles getting best of both worlds one month after trade deadline fire sale
articles.summary: The Orioles' trade deadline moves one month later are reason to celebrate.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles made the tough decision to conduct a fire sale at the MLB trade deadline, as they shipped out many of their key players at the deadline.

Adley Rutschman went to the Boston Red Sox , Taylor Ward was sent to the Seattle Mariners , and Tyler Wells went to the Tampa Bay Rays . It was a sell-off, and made with the belief this team wouldn't be contending.

However, since the August 3 deadline, the Orioles have gotten the best of both worlds. Johnny Flores Jr. of The Athletic gave the Orioles an "A" grade for their deadline moves one month later, as not only did they get some good prospects, but they're still contending.

Orioles get 'A' trade deadline re-grade amid contention and promising prospects

"Trade deadline report card: A," Flores writes. "... That the club is just one game back of the third and final AL wild-card spot, even after a busy Aug. 3, is all the more reason to celebrate."

Baltimore traded a few key players away and got back a massive selection of prospects in return. While losing Ward and Rutschman stings, the prospect capital so far has been good.

Anthony Eyanson, Kyson Witherspoon, Enddy Azocar, and Alex Hoppe, among others, have been great pickups for the Orioles.

But even with the big sell-off, the Orioles are just 1.5 games out of the third wild card spot on September 2. With one month to go in the 2026 regular season, the Orioles have a real chance of making the postseason.

This team sold at the trade deadline, shipping out Ward and Rutschman, two very good players. Yet, they've hung around in the Wild Card race enough to have a real chance to earn a playoff spot.

Funnily enough, the Mariners, who acquired Ward, are 5.5 out of the Wild Card and 5.0 back in the AL West right now. The Orioles, a team that sold at the deadline, have a better chance of making the postseason than a buyer does.

Selling at the deadline and still contending for a postseason spot is the best of both worlds for the Orioles. It was a productive deadline for the future, and it's not hurt the team's chances this season in the process. It's a massive win, deserving of this "A" grade.

articles.title: Jay Hill, Jason Beck assess each other's Michigan football schemes
articles.summary: Michigan football coordinators Jason Beck and Jay Hill are testing each other during camp to prepare for the season.
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. -- Michigan football had perhaps the best dual coordinator hires of the offseason in Jason Beck and Jay Hill, leading the offense and defense, respectively. And while they'll work to create headaches for opposing teams in just a few short days, the past several months, they've been creating headaches for each other.

The latest has come in fall camp, where each coordinator is working to ready his side of the ball. When the team goes good-on-good -- meaning the starting offense vs. the starting defense rather than against the scout team -- each is working to get the best of each other.

So, what does each side of the ball look like in each other's eyes?

Starting with the defense, Beck notes that there's a lot of moving parts and that can become problematic for all parties involved. It starts with confusing the quarterback, but the offensive line and the receivers also have to be mindful of what Hill's defense is doing on any given play.

"Very capable players, good players, very multiple front coverage," Beck said. "They do a really nice job disguising things on you. So you have to be dialed in with the fronts in the coverages because that is not a static thing. That's the same, play in and play out. So it taxes your whole line with their targeting. It taxes your pass protection with all your assignments.

"And then for the quarterback, that thing can change on the snap with what your reads and progressions are. So very capable in terms of the people, and also the scheme is a challenge."

Michigan football's biggest question at every position in 2026

The offense is perhaps the side of the ball most people are particularly excited about.

Beck oversaw the No. 4 offense in the country at two different schools in two successive years. Now, he's working to ensure that the third time isn't any different -- lest it be better.

Hill thinks that Michigan football fans will be elated when they see just how dynamic and explosive Beck's offense is, given all of the different wrinkles and schematic advantages it has.

"I can say this: Jason Beck's offense is awesome," Hill said. "And it's another one of those things where you better be prepared for the tempo and the physicality and all the zigging and zagging and everything that goes with it. I think the fans are going to love it, and the players are going to love it.

"Now we've got to go out and execute, but I'm excited to watch it in person and be on the other side of the ball of it. I have seen the offensive players just get better and better and better at their execution. That's probably a better question for Jason exactly where they're at, but I can't wait to watch it in person too. Going against it, it's tough to defend."

Fans will have a chance to see both the offense and defense in action on Saturday when the Wolverines host Western Michigan at The Big House.

articles.title: Everton gamble on Jack Grealish's return to form with second Manchester City loan
articles.summary: OPINION: Jack Grealish has returned to Everton on loan from Manchester City, and the England international will be hoping to rediscover his best form at the...
articles.body:
Jack Grealish is a charismatic presence and an exceptionally gifted player, but it's been quite some time since we've witnessed that exceptional gift in its full glory. Quite some time indeed.

Grealish quickly won over the Hill Dickinson faithful, which came as no surprise. It's extremely difficult not to warm to Jack.

And when he delivers the kind of performances he produced during the early stages of his Everton loan stint, that only enhances his appeal. At the new venue, Grealish provided a desperately needed touch of magic, as per The Mirror .

During his brief, initial stay, he represented the organization superbly, which he'll undoubtedly do again in his second stint at Hill Dickinson Stadium. However, by allocating significant resources to a second loan arrangement, Everton are still rolling the dice.

Grealish is a player who must demonstrate the brilliance remains intact, plain and simple. His campaign concluded last season in mid-January due to a stress fracture in his foot, but his 22-match period under David Moyes was generally considered to have been successful.

Yet that assessment was only accurate up to a certain extent. Following four assists in his opening three matches, Grealish then endured 14 Premier League games without registering another. In all, he found the net twice across 22 outings.

Numbers aren't the whole picture, but in Grealish's case, they carry weight. They don't capture the entire narrative, not by any stretch. However, they don't paint a completely false picture, either.

Grealish has featured in 20 Premier League matches in each of the past three campaigns, and across those 60 appearances, he's contributed six goals and eight assists. In what proved to be his second-to-last match last term, he received two late yellow cards for petulance during a home tie against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Moyes expressed frustration with him following that dismissal but clearly values what Grealish contributes both on the field and in the locker room. However, when he became the first British player to command a £100 million ($139 million) fee - back in August 2021 - few would have envisioned that the final two years of his six-year contract would involve loan spells elsewhere.

It represents a decline in fortunes, regardless of how it's portrayed. Yet Grealish only celebrates his 31st birthday next week and has ample opportunity to reestablish himself among the game's truly elite performers.

Everton have produced a fairly promising opening to the campaign, and despite the failure to land striker Folarin Balogun on deadline day, Grealish possesses the flair and exuberance to be central to a successful season for Moyes' side.

Moreover, he shouldn't lack for motivation. He understands he can rapidly become as beloved at Everton as he once was at Aston Villa.

Additionally, he has the prospect of an international comeback to pursue. That remains unlikely at present, but Thomas Tuchel is an admirer of his unpredictable talent and simply needs Grealish to demonstrate it consistently, week after week, across an extended stretch of time.

With just one year remaining on his Manchester City contract, Everton could consider themselves fortunate to secure Grealish for another loan stint. Yet the feeling is mutual — Grealish is equally fortunate to have landed at Hill Dickinson Stadium, because the winger still has a considerable amount to prove at the highest level.

articles.title: Leeds United Star Excited After Leaving The Club: Best Decision For The Whites?
articles.summary: Willy Gnonto has completed a season-long loan move from Leeds United to Fiorentina, with Inside Futbol first reporting the agreement before Leeds confirmed t...
articles.body:
Willy Gnonto has completed a season-long loan move from Leeds United to Fiorentina, with Inside Futbol first reporting the agreement before Leeds confirmed the transfer on 1 September. The 22-year-old Italian winger pushed for an exit after a frustrating 2025/26 campaign, when he made 23 Premier League appearances but played only 524 minutes. Fiorentina have an option to sign him permanently, reported at €15 million, while the wider package has been described elsewhere at €21 million.

Leeds United loan gives Willy Gnonto a fresh start

The switch nearly collapsed on deadline day because Leeds wanted another winger before releasing Gnonto. That condition cleared when the club agreed a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt's Jean-Matteo Bahoya, who joined on loan with an obligation to buy.

Gnonto then spoke proudly about joining Fiorentina, calling his first Serie A opportunity with the club a source of pride. He said his previous experiences had helped him grow and wanted to repay the faith shown by the president and coach.

Speaking to Fiorentina Official (via Firenze Viola ), he said: "This is my first experience in Serie A with the first team. Doing it at Fiorentina is a source of pride.

"I'm young, but I've still had a wealth of experiences that have helped me grow. I want to share them here.

"Yes, they [the president and coach] all welcomed me warmly.

"They're all good people and excited to see me. I hope to repay their faith on the pitch.

"I really wanted to be here, now comes the good part: I know what I can give and I want to make myself available to everyone."

Leeds United may regret a temporary exit

LONDON, ENGLAND – APRIL 05: Wilfried Gnonto of Leeds United reacts during the Emirates FA Cup Quarter Final match between West Ham United and Leeds United on April 05, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

For Gnonto, this move makes sense. His 2024/25 Championship season produced nine goals and six assists and earned him Leeds' Young Player of the Year award, yet promotion produced a very different picture. Last season brought 29 appearances across all competitions, but only one assist and no league goals, while his defensive work gave Daniel Farke another reason to limit his minutes.

A fresh start under Fabio Grosso could revive his confidence and Italy ambitions, especially after his senior international involvement and recent Under-21 appearances. Leeds United, meanwhile, could clear his wages and add another young winger in Bahoya, whose deal carries a reported €30 million mandatory package.

Given the £3.9 million Leeds paid for Gnonto, his upside always looked significant. The problem comes if Fiorentina decline their option after a strong season, because Leeds United could then face a player with reduced leverage, a year left on his contract and a much lower market value. That would leave the club wondering whether it should have pushed harder for a permanent sale in the first place.

articles.title: RB Jonathon Brooks out of practice with soreness, but Panthers unconcerned
articles.summary: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks remained out of practice on Wednesday, but head coach Dave Canales is unconcerned that Brooks' injury will keep him out...
articles.body:
Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks remained out of practice on Wednesday, but head coach Dave Canales is unconcerned that Brooks' injury will keep him out of the season opener.

"I'm very optimistic he'll be available for Week 1," Canales said Wednesday, via ESPN's Mike Kaye.

Brooks is dealing with "soreness" Canales revealed Tuesday, but Canales would not specify the location of Brooks' discomfort.

Brooks has undergone back-to-back ACL surgeries on his right knee, but he participated in all of training camp and two preseason games this summer. He played 17 snaps in the preseason.

He tore his right ACL against the Eagles in December 2024, a season after tearing it while playing for the University of Texas. Brooks missed all of the 2025 season.

In the three games he played as a rookie in 2024, Brooks had 12 touches for 45 yards.

Brooks is expected to complement Chuba Hubbard, with journeyman AJ Dillon also on the active roster. Trevor Etienne is on injured reserve with a designation to return as he works his way back from an ankle injury.

articles.title: Michigan hockey's latest outdoor game booked for storied NFL stadium
articles.summary: The game in February 2027 will be Michigan's 11th outdoor hockey game, most in college history.
articles.body:
Michigan hockey is taking it outside, again.

The Michigan hockey team will play an outdoor game at historic Lambeau Field, home of the Green Bay Packers, on Saturday, Feb. 20, 2027. Michigan will play Wisconsin in the game, with faceoff time to be announced.

This will mark the 11th outdoor game for Michigan hockey, the most in college history. Most recently, Michigan played Ohio State at Chicago's Wrigley Field in 2025 and Cleveland's FirstEnergy Stadium in 2023.

Michigan last played Wisconsin outdoors in 2010, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin.

Lambeau Field will celebrate its 70th anniversary in 2027. It last hosted an outdoor hockey game in 2006, when Wisconsin beat Ohio State, 4-2, in the inaugural "Frozen Tundra Hockey Classic."

General-public tickets for the 2027 game will go on sale Friday, Sept. 11.

Michigan hockey opens the 2026-27 season Oct. 2 at home against Bowling Green. The Wolverines are coming off a 38-8-1 season, which included another appearance in the Frozen Four .

articles.title: Steelers have a 'complicated' problem they need to address
articles.summary: It's not just about Aaron Rodgers with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
The word "complicated" isn't one you want to hear when it comes to NFL projections. Ideally, your favorite team won't have a complicated situation. But, the Pittsburgh Steelers have quite the complex problem on their hands as the upcoming season unfolds.

This issue has nothing to do with their quarterback situation. Of course, the Steelers have Aaron Rodgers locked in for the next year, so they're good for the next season. But, after that, they'll have to figure out their signal-caller situation. That's not now, though.

On Wednesday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN unleashed a feature with a roster of NFL players to keep an eye on next offseason if they don't sign extensions. These are guys to watch closely throughout the season .

Joey Porter Jr.'s contract situation with the Pittsburgh Steelers is complicated

With the Steelers, he says they are dealing with a "complicated" contract situation with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. He's not sugarcoating it, either.

"This is probably the most complicated of them all. Momentum for a deal just hasn't been there," he says in the piece. "My sense is the player has been frustrated that, despite his status as a high-level man corner, he hasn't been made a priority."

He adds that the "2023 draft picks getting paid by Pittsburgh, linebacker Nick Herbig and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton, who received four-year extensions this summer, play smaller roles."

Fowler adds that the Steelers didn't give him a formal offer, which may have sent a message to Porter that they want him to play out the last year of his rookie deal, "which prompted him to consider the possibility of a trade or sitting out for an extended period." He skipped the practice field but was back this week.

Fowler also says that the coaching staff is "all-in on his ability as a high-level cover man," so that's not the issue. Time will tell how this shakes out, but it's definitely murky, at best.

articles.title: Biggest question marks for Colorado football entering 2026 season
articles.summary: From Julian Lewis to the running game, Buffaloes Wire examines the biggest questions facing Colorado football entering the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Colorado has a ton of roster turnover heading into the 2026 college football season, which often brings plenty of question marks. Still, in the age of the transfer portal, they probably should be labeled unknowns rather than question marks. Two new coordinators, a new offensive scheme, and plenty of new players make the 2026 Buffs a very intriguing team entering the season.

How good will Colorado's offense be at averaging 30-plus points? Can the defense finally be a better unit against the run? Those are all some of the questions Buffs fans may have entering the 2026 season. Our staff at Buffaloes Wire put together our thoughts on the biggest question facing Colorado football this fall.

How productive can Colorado's run game become?

Ariana Pensy: The quality of the run game remains the biggest question mark going into this season. Last year, their leading rusher did not even reach 400 yards, and their quarterback, Kaidon Salter, led the team in rushing touchdowns. Colorado took to the transfer portal to address this issue by adding Damian Henderson Jr from Colorado State and Richard Young from Alabama. DeKalon Taylor will also be returning after missing eight games last season due to injury. They should have enough talent to make the run game decent this year, but it remains a major concern given the uncertainty of relying on so many transfers.

James Carnes: I need to see if Colorado will establish a true run game this season to stay ahead of the chains and avoid long passing downs. What we've heard from fall camp is that it is one of Brennan Marion's focuses.

Can Julian Lewis be the player Colorado needs?

Charlie Strella: An offense cannot be productive without a quarterback who can distribute the ball efficiently. Lewis showed in small samples last year that he is an accurate thrower and not one who puts the ball in harm's way. How big a step Lewis takes this year likely determines how far the Buffaloes can go. If he lives up to his five-star recruit hype, CU's offense will be one of the Big 12's best.
