articles.title: Steelers sign former Titans safety, round out practice squad
articles.summary: Pittsburgh’s initial 2026 practice squad is up to 17 players.
articles.body:
By announcing the signing of safety Bishop Fitzgerald on Wednesday, the Steelers have officially filled all 17 spots on their 2026 practice squad ahead of the regular season.

According to Steelers.com, the initial squad is as follows, with outside linebacker Julius Welschof filling the International Player Pathway Program exemption slot:

OLB Julius Welschof (International Player Pathway Program exemption)

Three players: Fitzgerald, Swinson and Vigers, are new to the Steelers organization.

Fitzgerald was an undrafted free agent in 2026, spending the summer with the Tennessee Titans. Playing college football at NC State and USC, Fitzgerald recorded his best collegiate seasons in 2025 with the Trojans, when he logged five interceptions alongside 51 total tackles.

The 5'11, 201-pound safety ran a 4.55-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine. Pre-draft, NFL.com analyst Lance Zierlein described Fitzgerald as a "compact, ballhawking safety prospect with alignment versatility," noting he's much better defending the pass than diagnosing the run.

Vigers went undrafted in 2025 out of UL Monroe, spending time on the Washington Commanders' practice squad last season. In his final collegiate season in 2024, the 6'2, 200-pound corner logged 38 total tackles and one interception. He scored an 8.00 RAS with a reported 4.52-second 40-yard dash.

Swinson is the most interesting name of the bunch as a former fifth-round pick by the New England Patriots in 2025. He appeared in three games for the Patriots last season, recording one tackle. In his final collegiate season at LSU in 2024, he recorded 8.5 sacks along with 59 total tackles.

Zierlein described Swinson as a "late bloomer with big hands, long arms and a frame to carry more muscle" pre-draft, adding he's "competitive at the point of attack, where he uses his length and footwork to beat the block or prevent block sustains." Zierlein noted Swinson still needed to work on rushing strategies and improving quickness, but had the upside to be a starting outside linebacker in a 3-4.

Interestingly, the Steelers' initial practice squad does not include the reported signing of former Cowboys safety Juanyeh Thomas. The planned deal was reported by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday, and seemingly confirmed by Thomas making a string of Steelers-related posts on X afterwards. For now, Thomas is not listed on Pittsburgh's roster or practice squad.

articles.title: Did Bill Guerin hint at Wild's next targets if he can't extend Quinn Hughes?
articles.summary: Guerin's comments about No. 1 centers caught the attention of hockey fans in Canada.
articles.body:
The Wild have been locked into negotiations with star defenseman Quinn Hughes all summer. Despite both sides saying they would like to extend the relationship past this upcoming season, so far no deal has been finalized, with just under a month until the regular season begins.

Wild GM Bill Guerin said in several interviews at the State Fair on Monday that he was "confident" an extension would be worked out.

However, an answer to a separate line of questioning has caught the ears of those in Canada. Guerin's remarks about the team's center position may have given us an insight into his targets if he fails to secure a Hughes extension.

When asked by KFAN's Dan Barreiro on Monday if he believes he has a No. 1 center, Guerin responded, "I like to think (Joel Eriksson Ek) is a No. 1 center. I think ideally he is the No. 2 center in the game."

It was the next part of Guerin's quote that sent warning signs to several teams across the border.

"When you talk about No. 1 centers, you're talking about (Connor) McDavid and (Auston) Matthews. And guys like that, they just don't come around all that often," said Guerin. "Look, centers, they're tough to come by. (At) any level. Honestly, we're talking about depth guys, and we need centers. They're just hard to come by."

Guerin name-dropping McDavid and Matthews out of the blue set off alarm bells in Canada.

"To any hockey fan of the Leafs or Oilers who just heard that, you need to realize something, in this moment," said Toronto sports talk host Sid Seixeiro. "If you weren't that interested in the Quinn Hughes story, you better get interested. Because you now are really rooting for the Minnesota Wild to sign this guy to a massive deal, and get out of the free agent market in two years' time. Because, arguably, the most aggressive GM in hockey, in an unsolicited way, brought up two guys in Matthews and McDavid, who are about to be free agents in less than two years.

"If they don't sign Quinn Hughes in Minnesota, that money from owner Craig Leipold is sitting right there on the table. You better hope they sign Quinn Hughes in Minnesota, or there's going to be an added market problem to Matthews' free agency, and McDavid's, that you might not have seen coming. And it's not that far away in Minnesota."

This isn't the first time Guerin has mentioned Matthews. After the trade deadline passed in March, Guerin told TSN Radio in Canada, "I think the world of him."

Matthews captained the United States men's hockey team to a gold medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Turin, Italy. Guerin was the general manager who constructed the U.S. roster.

While the Wild have been searching for an agreement with Hughes on a long-term extension, they also have been in the hunt for a No. 1 center. That hunt has frequently focused on Detroit's Dylan Larkin, who requested a trade back in June.

Notably, Guerin refused in the three interviews he did at the fair on Monday to discuss the ongoing trade talks with Detroit. However, as the situation has evolved over the summer, it appears less and less likely that Minnesota, by itself, has the pieces to pull off a trade for the Red Wings captain.

If the Wild can't land Larkin, and somehow miss out on retaining Hughes, then Guerin's eyes will almost certainly look towards the next big fish he can land.

Matthews is in a bit of an interesting situation in Toronto, where the Maple Leafs are seemingly in the midst of another overhaul. At 28, how likely is it that one of the league's best centers, in the league's most hockey-crazed market, is going to want to sit through a rebuild?

Matthews has two years left on his current deal that pays out $13.25 million annually. If the Wild don't have the pieces to pull off a trade for Larkin, there's an even lower chance they have the pieces to swing a trade for a player of Matthews' caliber.

They would almost certainly need a third team involved. Or they hold on to the cash and shell out a massive contract to Matthews, who becomes a free agent ahead of his age-30 season.

McDavid, 29, has gotten close to hoisting the Stanley Cup with Edmonton. The Oilers have been to the finals in two of the last three seasons and fallen short both times. Last offseason, McDavid signed a two-year extension for well below market value to stay in Edmonton and extend their window.

However, that also is a sign that McDavid could be looking elsewhere if the Oilers can't get over the hump in the next two seasons.

Guerin has shown he's willing to be aggressive when it comes to improving the Wild. If a Hughes extension fails to materialize, then all eyes turn to what Minnesota's GM does next.

articles.title: Drake announces plans to unveil Johnny Bright statue
articles.summary: Drake University will unveil a statue of Johnny Bright on Oct. 16 at 11 a.m.
articles.body:
Drake will honor one of its most prominent and influential former football players later this season.

Bulldogs director of athletics Brian Hardin announced the school will unveil a statue of Johnny Bright in a public ceremony on Oct. 16 at 11 a.m.

The statue will stand approximately six and a half feet tall and rest on a one-foot-tall concrete pedestal outside the southeast gate of Drake Stadium, along Forest Avenue.

Bright suffered a broken jaw after he was repeatedly struck after a play during Drake's Oct. 20, 1951 game at Oklahoma State.

Two Des Moines Register photographers caught the incident that garnered national attention and earned the Pulitzer Prize. Bright went on to earn All-American honors that season and finished fifth in the Heisman Trophy voting.

"We are immensely proud at Drake Athletics to have helped bring a statue celebrating Johnny Bright to our campus," Hardin said in a statement. "His life story of valor, honor, persistence, and selflessness will undoubtedly inspire others. The location of the statue and the plaques that will share details of Johnny will certainly become a destination for visitors to our campus."

articles.title: Spurs Jackals' new 18-and-up age requirement has fans split ahead of upcoming season
articles.summary: Spurs fans are debating the Jackals' new 18-and-up membership requirement as the supporter section prepares to expand for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs ' most boisterous fan section is getting bigger next season, but younger fans won't be part of the pack.

The Spurs Jackals will require members to be at least 18 years old for the 2026-27 season, a change that has prompted debate online over whether children should be excluded from the supporter group.

Founded with the help of Spurs star Victor Wembanyama ahead of the 2025-26 season, the Jackals are expanding their "Lair" across Sections 114 and 115 at Frost Bank Center and adding 100 members. Auditions for new members are scheduled for 9 a.m. Sept. 19.

The new age requirement has drawn criticism from some fans online.

"Bad call imo. Spurs are a family franchise," one fan wrote on X. "The super-fan section should reflect that."

Another fan questioned why the group would raise the age requirement and force younger members out.

The Jackals responded to the criticism on X, saying the decision followed an evaluation of the group's inaugural season.

"It was a tough choice for sure, we love our kid Jackals, but as the Jackals have and will continue to grow, the atmosphere will become more intense, with constant standing, chanting, and coordinated movement and support," the group wrote. "After evaluating the past season, we feel an 18+ environment is the best fit for the direction of the section."

Fans offered several alternatives, including creating a "Junior Jackals" program that would allow children to participate during select weekend games.

Others defended the change. One fan compared the Jackals to supporter groups associated with European soccer clubs, arguing that children can grow up with the fandom before eventually joining the section as adults.

Some fans, however, questioned whether an adults-only rule was necessary to create a more intense atmosphere and argued that the supporter section should remain open to younger Spurs fans.

Jackals member Raylyn Boyson, who is known online as "Raylien," also weighed in, saying she understood the frustration surrounding the change.

Boyson said one young member at the center of the online discussion had been an "incredible Jackal" who represented the group well. She also noted that she will have to reaudition and is not guaranteed a spot next season.

Boyson welcomed some of the alternatives proposed by fans and said she would be willing to present those ideas if she returns to the group.

"I would love to present some of the suggestions and solutions brought up," Boyson wrote on X. "We should be more solution-oriented and less about pointing fingers."

She also suggested there could be more to the decision.

"Knowing the Spurs, I'm sure it goes deeper than just not wanting kids," Boyson wrote.

Wembanyama helped launch the supporter section ahead of the 2025-26 season, taking inspiration from the passionate fan groups common in European sports. The Jackals dress in Spurs gear, pound drums, stand throughout games and lead chants to create additional energy at home games.

About 100 prospective members auditioned for the inaugural group in September 2025, with Wembanyama helping judge the applicants.

Those hoping to join this season must commit to attending at least 75% of eligible Spurs preseason and regular-season home games, participate in chants and rituals, support the team "with passion and respect" and help create a safe, inclusive and positive environment.

Membership costs $999 per person and provides access to tickets for preseason and regular-season home games. Members also receive exclusive gear, a 15% discount at the Spurs Fan Shop and access to special meetups. The Spurs have reported the same price and general benefits for the 2026-27 season.

articles.body:
Bradley Barcola Deal Offers Major Clue Over Bhatia and Liverpool Investors

Bradley Barcola's arrival at Liverpool was already one of the defining deals of the transfer window. Yet the involvement of Amit Bhatia has added another dimension to the story, with questions now surrounding what his role might indicate about Liverpool's investors and the club's future ownership.

Speaking to Dave Davis on Anfield Index's Media Matters podcast, Liverpool reporter David Lynch described Bhatia's involvement in the Barcola transfer as "really interesting".

For Lynch, its significance potentially extends beyond Liverpool securing one of their major attacking targets.

Bhatia Involvement Catches Lynch's Attention

Discussing reports that Bhatia played a role in completing the Barcola deal, Lynch immediately connected the development to Liverpool's evolving ownership situation.

"I guess again it kind of tells you really that, you know, the direction I think that ownership move is going in," Lynch told Davis.

Lynch suggested Bhatia may have been learning more about how Liverpool operate at the highest level of the transfer market.

"Maybe, you know, it's almost like shadowing a little bit of Mike Gordon to kind of see exactly how, you know, it might work."

Bhatia's previous experience in football was also highlighted.

"He knows how football works," Lynch said. "But I mean, we are talking about a crazy level, aren't we? Of kind of, you know, the deals, the biggest deals you could do in football."

Barcola certainly falls into that category. Liverpool have added a player Lynch has previously described as an "incredibly exciting signing", with the France international strengthening Iraola's attacking options.

Liverpool Investors Could Assume Greater Influence

Bhatia's participation becomes particularly intriguing when placed alongside Lynch's expectations for what could eventually happen at Liverpool.

"These responsibilities ultimately, if this does go the way we expect, are probably going to fall to him," Lynch said.

"He's going to be that Mike Gordon figure in the future."

That is a significant observation. Lynch sees Bhatia being hands on during the Barcola negotiations as potentially valuable experience ahead of assuming greater responsibility.

"Probably best to kind of see and be hands on in that moment."

Liverpool's ownership situation has already been a major subject on Media Matters, with Lynch previously discussing the prospect of significant changes involving FSG and incoming investors.

January Could Provide Another Bhatia Clue

Attention will inevitably turn towards the January transfer window and whether Bhatia becomes increasingly visible around Liverpool's recruitment operation.

"If they do any business in the January transfer window, then that's going to be, you know, a big kind of thing where Bhatia will be even more involved," Lynch said.

Liverpool will also have a new sporting director by that stage, according to the discussion, potentially creating another change within the club's football operation.

Lynch stopped short of claiming an ownership transition was guaranteed, stressing that the mechanism might exist without necessarily being used.

"Only they can know that at the moment. I'm not, you know, that mechanism is there, whether they exploit it or not, I haven't got a clue."

Yet Bhatia's participation in one of Liverpool's biggest transfers was enough to attract Lynch's attention.

"I thought it's really, really interesting that he was so heavily involved in that."

Barcola may therefore represent more than a major addition for Iraola. His transfer has provided another fascinating glimpse into the people increasingly operating around Liverpool's biggest decisions, with Bhatia's involvement now something worth watching as the club moves towards January.

articles.title: Ukrainian Player Confirms She Quit LSU Because Kim Mulkey Signed Russian
articles.summary: Kate Koval says she wants to play somewhere else this year.
articles.body:
Former LSU women's basketball player Kate Koval, who is Ukrainian, said Wednesday she quit Kim Mulkey's team last week because the program signed a Russian player.

Koval said in an Instagram post she learned Mulkey planned to sign 17-year-old Russian pro Anna Minaeva in April, "several days after the transfer portal had closed," a situation that made her "question whether LSU remained the right place for me." Koval said she is withdrawing from LSU, which Front Office Sports reported last week.

Koval said she hopes the NCAA "recognizes" and "understands" her situation, and that she will be allowed to play basketball somewhere else during the upcoming 2026–27 season. The NCAA forbids midyear basketball transfers from playing if they were enrolled at another school during the first semester; Koval quit the team the day before classes started.

The NCAA and LSU did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Mulkey announced last week that Koval, a junior from Kyiv, came to her on Aug. 23 to quit the team for "personal reasons," nine days after the school announced Minaeva's signing.

Koval was set to be the starting center for the Tigers this year after playing in all 35 games for LSU last season and starting 17. She spent her first season at Notre Dame before transferring to Baton Rouge.

Ukraine and Russia have been at war since February 2022. Koval's father, Oleksandr, is a drone operator in the conflict.

"For me, this war is not distant or abstract," Koval said in her social media post on Wednesday. "People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes."

Mulkey told The Advocate that she had a conversation with Koval about Minaeva during the recruiting process.

"Know that what I have to do in this business, I cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries," Mulkey told The Advocate she recalled telling Koval. Mulkey also said she suggested the two players could maybe even help end the war, to which Koval replied: "I doubt that."

articles.title: Shankland brace at Falkirk gives Rangers back-to-back league wins
articles.summary: Rangers make it back-to-back wins in the Scottish Premiership as Lawrence Shankland's superb double downs wasteful Falkirk.
articles.body:
Rangers made it back-to-back wins in the Scottish Premiership as Lawrence Shankland's superb double downed wasteful Falkirk.

The Scotland striker scored either side of Kosta Nedeljkovic's own goal to alleviate pressure on Derek McInnes - who watched from the stands amid his touchline ban - and build some much-needed momentum for the Ibrox outfit.

After scoring the winner at Pittodrie on Sunday, Shankland fired Rangers in front on eight minutes with a fine touch and strike after being teed up by Djeidi Gassama.

It was reflective of a slick start by McInnes' team and Kim Min-Su went close to his first Rangers goal soon after as his low drive bounced clear off the base of a post.

However, Falkirk grew into the contest and Rangers started to make sloppy errors, which culminated in an equaliser just before half-time.

Cammy Devlin coughed up possession in midfield, Ethan Ross skinned Olwethu Makhanya down the right and his low cross was turned into his own net by Aston Villa loanee Nedeljkovic.

Falkirk had several golden opportunities to hit the front after the break, with American striker Jacob Murrell twice shooting straight at Ivor Pandur when he should have scored.

And the hosts were made to pay for their profligacy as Shankland took Ross McCrorie's pass in his stride before sweeping another clinical left-footed finish into the bottom corner.

Falkirk remain without a league win and are only above pointless Kilmarnock, while Rangers are fifth on seven points from their four matches.

articles.title: How Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman support each other's pro careers
articles.summary: Soccer star Trinity Rodman and tennis star Ben Shelton share how Instagram sparked their relationship and how they manage long distance.
articles.body:
Trinity Rodman and Ben Shelton's relationship started with an Instagram message.

"I said, 'You're sick ... fire emoji,'" Rodman recalled on Kylie Kelce's "Not Gonna Lie" podcast earlier this month. "(Shelton) responded and was like, 'Yeah, you were sick at the Olympics too.' Yeah. That happened. He matched the cringe situation. And then I think maybe a week or two later we met in person."

Rodman, an Olympic gold medalist in soccer, and Shelton, the top American male singles player in tennis, first announced their relationship in March 2025 on – you guessed it – Instagram. The couple have been inseparable ever since, showing up and supporting each other at their respective sporting events.

Rodman and Shelton are superstar athletes in their own regard. But together, they are one of the leading power couples in sports.

Rodman was the youngest player to be drafted in National Women's Soccer League history at the time at age 18, and she led the Washington Spirit to their first NWSL championship as a rookie in 2021. She also helped Team USA win Olympic gold at the 2024 Paris Games.

Shelton is currently ranked No. 9 in the world on the ATP Tour and is the No. 8 seed at this year's US Open. He has seven career titles under his belt with a 144–90 career record. Shelton has yet to win a Grand Slam, but he's knocking on the door with multiple major semifinal appearances.

Despite each athlete navigating their own grueling schedule that often finds them in different places (or continents) any given time of the year, Shelton and Rodman find time to support each other's goals.

"It's definitely hard ... it's like, 'Oh my gosh, we don't get to see each other at all," Rodman told USA TODAY Sports. "We are so good at understanding each other's schedules and the way we operate and times when we need advice, times when we don't. So going through that together has been amazing."

Rodman added, "I think we're always so good at supporting each other. And yeah, just being individuals as well, I think has been huge for us of not getting so blended together."

Rodman was on hand for Shelton's 1-6, 6-1, 7-6(3), 6-2 first-round win over Tallon Griekspoor on Monday and his 6-3, 5-7, 7-6(3), 6-5 second-round victory against Hubert Hurkacz Wednesday, Sept. 2, where she wore a "I (heart) my boyfriend" shirt.

Earlier, Rodman recently surprised Shelton at the 2026 Canadian Open, which he won for the second consecutive year. Ahead of Shelton's fourth-round match, Rodman flew to Montreal after the Washington Spirit's 4-3 loss to the North Carolina Courage in Washington, D.C. She called supporting her beau, "the best feeling in the world."

"I think to know we're both on the grind, running our bodies to the ground, always exhausted, doing what we love, and then to also be able to be a little WAG in a sense, it feels so good for us," Rodman told Kelce. "We do enjoy it a lot because I don't ... look at him and I'm like, 'He's an athlete.' I look at him like that's my rock. And every time I do something, I just love to be able to look at him and know that we're on the same page thinking something."

When Rodman attended Shelton's Stuttgart Open win in June, he called Rodman his "good luck charm."

"I want to thank my girlfriend for flying here from Brazil," Shelton said on the podium. "I won a title at I think every tournament she's been at this year. ... I really appreciate you making the effort."

The support is mutual. Shelton attended the Spirit's 2-1 win over the Houston Dash on July 3, where Rodman scored two goals, including a game-winner in stoppage time. Following the winning goal, Rodman ran over to the stands to share a celebratory kiss with Shelton.

The Tennis Channel labeled Shelton and Rodman the most athletic couple in the country, but Rodman was hesitant to claim the title. She pointed to a pair of basektball stars – the Las Vegas Aces' Aja Wilson and Miami Heat's Bam Adebayo – adding, "I would be scared to play the same sport, because I feel like if Ben (Shelton) were to say anything coachable, I would lose my mind."

articles.title: Three goals and three points for the Hoops at Paradise
articles.summary: Scottish PremiershipWednesday, September 2, 2026Celtic ParkCELTIC…3(Duran 14, Nygren 34, Yang 45+1)ABERDEEN…0 Celtic picked up another three Premiership poin...
articles.body:
Scottish PremiershipWednesday, September 2, 2026Celtic Park

CELTIC…3 (Duran 14, Nygren 34, Yang 45+1)

Celtic picked up another three Premiership points this evening with a comfortable 3-0 win against Aberdeen at Celtic Park, as Camilo Durán, Benjamin Nygren and Yang all found the back of the net in the first half to put the game beyond the visitors.

With less than 15 minutes played, Camilo Durán fired Celtic into the lead with a finish straight out of the top drawer to claim his fifth goal in six matches.

Benjamin Nygren picked the Colombian out on the edge of the box, and Durán needed no invitation to have a strike at goal as he thundered a shot in to the top corner of the net to make it 1-0.

Durán found himself with a good chance to double Celtic's lead and grab his second of the night with just over 20 minutes gone when Benjamin Nygren slipped a clever pass through to him on the edge of the area, but this time the Aberdeen keeper was equal to the effort.

In the opening half-hour of the match, the ball belonged almost exclusively to Celtic, with Yang and Haissem Hassan providing a threat on either wing. Both men almost linked up to make it 2-0, but Hassan's effort from close range was blocked before it could trouble the goalkeeper.

With 30 minutes on the clock, Nesta Guinness-Walker hit the target for the visitors from distance, but Viljami Sinisalo was equal to it and was able to make the save comfortably.

In the 34th minute, Celtic's lead was doubled by Benjamin Nygren, who extended his brilliant record of having scored against Aberdeen every time he has played against them.

Haissem Hassan whipped a dangerous cross into the box which Camilo Durán tried to control. Although he was unable to make contact, the Colombian's presence caused confusion for the Dons' defence and a deflection carried the ball straight to Nygren, who coolly finished to make it 2-0.

The visitors came close to pulling a goal back in stoppage time at the end of the half when Gavin Molloy rattled the crossbar with a header after a well-taken corner, and to add insult to injury for the visitors, from that miss the Hoops broke forward at pace and bagged a third goal.

Camilo Durán raced down the right wing in pursuit of the ball and sent a good pass towards Yang who was composed as he found the bottom corner and made it 3-0 just before half time.

Celtic began the second half with the same intensity they had shown in the opening 45 minutes, and just moments after the restart Haissem Hassan sent a good effort towards goal from distance, but the ball rose just over the bar.

The visitors, despite the game being beyond them, continued to hunt for some sort of route back in to the game and just before the hour mark Conor Ronan crossed a good ball towards the back post, but Colby Donovan was on hand to head the danger clear.

Soon after, Martin O'Neill made his first changes of the evening, bringing Benjamin Nygren and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain off for Mika Baur and Oliver Sørensen, with the latter making his Celtic debut after joining the club yesterday.

There was another debut for the Hoops this evening, with Shumaira Mhueka coming on for his first appearance. James Forrest and Sebastian Tounekti were also brought on, with Camilo Durán, Yang and Haissem Hassan all coming off.

Mhueka, who only joined Celtic on loan from Chelsea today, tested the keeper just moments after coming on, drawing a good save from Marius Müller after showing some quick feet to open up an opportunity.

With five minutes to go, Mika Baur almost found the bottom corner from 30 yards out, firing a low shot to the Aberdeen keeper's right, which Müller done well to keep out considering the torrential rain that was battering Celtic Park.

James Forrest went close to extending his incredible scoring run to 18 consecutive seasons near the end of the match with a powerful effort from close range, but once again the visitors' keeper was on hand to make the save.

articles.title: Fury calls Joshua a 'coward' as wait for announcement continues
articles.summary: Tyson Fury says Anthony Joshua is a "coward" as the pair face a tense wait to see whether their long-awaited all-British heavyweight blockbuster can be agree...
articles.body:
Tyson Fury has labelled Anthony Joshua a "coward" as the pair face a tense wait to see whether their long-awaited all-British heavyweight bout can be agreed.

The long-time rivals had been expected to finally settle their differences and face off in November, but the likelihood of that happening is diminishing as an agreement over the venue has yet to be reached.

Two-time unified world champion Joshua and his Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn have signed a contract for the fight to take place in the United Kingdom, while the fight's organisers are understood to favour staging it in the United States.

Hearn has previously said the contracts would have to be renegotiated if the fight were to take place outside the United Kingdom.

On Wednesday, Fury, who defeated journeyman Mariusz Wach last month to keep the potential blockbuster clash with Joshua on track, said negotiations over the fight were becoming "quite tiring".

"I've been down to fight at every location that's been mentioned - England, Ireland, Vegas, New York, back to England, back to Ireland, back to New York," said the 38-year-old.

"Listen, I've said yep, yep, yep, yep, yep, every single time. Zero stipulations.

"The facts are I feel like you're being a coward. I feel like you don't want the fight and you're just conning everybody. I feel like you've been doing that for years.

"You've had many opportunities to fight me, but deep down you've never really wanted it, so let's see if you're going to man up for a final time."

In a separate post, Fury continued to taunt Joshua, 36, this time alongside former heavyweight champion Mike Tyson, telling his fellow Brit to "sign the contract, big boy" as he paid homage to Tyson's iconic line.

Queensbury's Frank Warren, who promotes Fury, told Sky Sports News his fighter was "100%" signed up for the fight.

"It is signed by Tyson," said Warren. "Tyson is signed up for the fight and agreed for the fight."

articles.title: WWE Armchair Booker: 5 ‘Would You?’ Questions, Including an Alexa Bliss Turn
articles.summary: WWE’s roster is deeper than it has been in years, and the booking sheet coming out of SummerSlam shows it. […]
articles.body:
WWE's roster is deeper than it has been in years, and the booking sheet coming out of SummerSlam shows it. CM Punk is carrying the Undisputed WWE Championship on SmackDown. Roman Reigns holds the World Heavyweight Championship on Raw. Solo Sikoa has become the most over act on either brand. Kevin Owens is back after 17 months away with a neck injury and already has an argument for another title shot.

The problem sits on the other side of the card. Punk and Cody Rhodes at SummerSlam was a battle of a babyface against a babyface. Reigns and Seth Rollins were the same. Sikoa is a babyface, LA Knight is a babyface, and Randy Orton returned as a heel and got cheered anyway. Sami Zayn blasting both Punk and Owens with the title belt in Toronto was the first real attempt to fix that.

So there are plenty of creative changes that can be made soon. With that in mind, we ask about five adjustments that should be considered. Each of these is a decision WWE could make on television inside the next few months. None of them require a signing, a trade, or a budget. They only require someone in the writers' room to pull the trigger.

Would you turn Alexa Bliss against Charlotte Flair?

Alexa Bliss pitched this pairing herself, and she has been open about why it works. Speaking on Busted Open Radio, Bliss described the appeal of the run with Charlotte Flair as getting to see "both of us letting our guards down and having fun." The two held the Women's Tag Team Championships for 100 days and have since added Tatum Paxley to the group on SmackDown, where they are working opposite Jade Cargill , Michin and B-Fab.

The turn is coming eventually. Bliss has spent her entire main roster career stabbing partners in the back, and she has said as much, which means the audience is already waiting for it. That is exactly the reason to hold it. The Bliss pairing has given Flair something she has not had in close to a decade, which is a version of her character the crowd actually wants to cheer. Cash that in now for one hot segment, and WWE loses the babyface Flair and gets a heel turn everybody saw coming. Save it for when Flair is back in a singles championship program, and the betrayal costs her a title.

Would you make Tiffany Stratton the next Chelsea Green program?

Sportsnaut answer: Yes, and it should happen before Rhea Ripley comes back.

Chelsea Green won the Interim WWE Women's Championship in the five-woman ladder match at SummerSlam, and she got there by knocking Tiffany Stratton off the ladder with a Swanton. Since then, the two have been booked as friends. Green came out with a kendo stick to run off Nia Jax and Lash Legend after they attacked Stratton, and the pair have teamed against Fatal Influence for the Women's Tag Team Championships.

The story is already written. Stratton is the Women's United States Champion; she was the favorite going into that ladder match in her home state, and she lost the title shot because her friend took her off a ladder. Green does not have to do anything villainous for that to curdle. The complication is Rhea Ripley , whose return sets up a unification match that is the obvious finish to the interim reign. Run Stratton first. Give Green a defense with real emotional stakes, then send her into Ripley having already been tested.

Would you have Solo Sikoa dethrone Roman Reigns?

Sportsnaut answer: Book the match. Do not change the title.

Sikoa hit Reigns with a Samoan Spike on the Aug. 17 episode of Raw and refused to rejoin the Bloodline, which was the payoff to a turn that has worked better than almost anyone expected. He and Knight beat the Usos and Jacob Fatu at SummerSlam alongside Royce Keys, and the reaction has been strong enough that WWE has kept feeding him television time on both brands.

Reigns against Sikoa is a main event, and it should happen. Putting the World Heavyweight Championship on Sikoa in the next few months is a different question, and the answer is no. His run as a top babyface is a few months old. The Raw title picture already has Oba Femi and Bron Breakker positioned as the next generation, and Reigns dropping the belt to Sikoa now would burn the biggest chase story WWE has developed this year. Let Sikoa fail first. The Rumble season is the right window.

Would you make SmackDown three hours permanently?

SmackDown moved to three hours in January 2026 and dropped back to two hours in the second half of the year, which is the same cycle the show ran in 2025. WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select has reported that USA Network sources expect the show to expand again in January 2027. That is a network scheduling decision built around lead-in programming, not a creative one.

The two-hour version is the better show. WWE already produces roughly eight hours of weekly television between Raw on Netflix, NXT on The CW, and SmackDown on USA, before premium live events are added. Locking SmackDown at three hours every week does not create more stars; it creates more segments that have to be filled. The current arrangement gives WWE the extra inventory when the network needs it and gives the writers a tighter show the rest of the year. That is the better of the two options.

Would you have Kevin Owens dethrone CM Punk?

Sportsnaut answer: Yes, but not in the rematch, and not next.

Owens returned at SummerSlam after 17 months out, won a fatal four-way over Zayn, Gunther , and Finn Balor, and got his shot in Toronto on the Aug. 21 SmackDown. He lost it when Zayn slid the title into the ring, Owens refused to use it, and Zayn hit him with it instead. Punk retained. Owens has as clean a case for a rematch as anyone gets.

The title is not the story WWE built there, though. Zayn turning on Owens after Owens refused to cheat is the most valuable thing to come out of that main event, and it gave the roster the top heel it has been short of all year. Run Owens against Zayn first and let it be personal. If Owens comes out of that program hot, then put him in with Punk again and change the title. A championship win in his first month back would be a return that has years of mileage left in it.

Four of these five questions are about the same shortage. WWE has more likeable performers than it can fit on a card, and almost nobody the audience wants to see lose. Punk against Rhodes, Reigns against Rollins, Sikoa against the Bloodline, and Owens against Punk were all built as good guy against good guy, and the company had to bring Orton back and turn Zayn just to give the top of the card an opposing side.

That is why the Bliss turn and the Stratton turn are worth holding rather than rushing. Turns work when they are earned and when the person turning has somewhere to go afterward. WWE has spent 2026 proving it can build babyfaces from scratch. Sikoa went from a stale enforcer character to the most over act on the roster in about three months. The harder job is the other half of the equation, and both Bliss and Stratton are sitting on stories that could fill it if the company gives them a reason beyond needing a heel that week.

The SmackDown question is the outlier, and it is the one where the answer is easiest. Three hours is a revenue decision that WWE and USA Network will keep making on a schedule that has nothing to do with the wrestling. Fans do not have to pretend it is a creative upgrade.

articles.summary: A Harry Kane double helped holders Bayern Munich come from a goal down to win 4-1 in their German Cup opener at second division Osnabrueck on Wednesday. Baye...
articles.body:
A Harry Kane double helped holders Bayern Munich come from a goal down to win 4-1 in their German Cup opener at second division Osnabrueck on Wednesday.

Tom Bischof and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet as Bayern struck back after trailing early on when the hosts struck through a superb Robin Meissner strike.

"It's never easy at an away ground with a very good atmosphere. They started the game with an amazing goal, and we had to stay calm," Kane said.

England captain Kane now has 148 goals in 150 games in all competitions for Bayern Munich, whom he joined from boyhood side Tottenham in 2023.

Meissner had the hosts dreaming of a shock upset when he scored with a lovely dipping shot from outside the box after just five minutes.

Bayern, the 21-time German Cup winners, were last eliminated at the first round in 1994 and quickly levelled things up when Kane hammered home a rebound.

Bischof added another in similar fashion six minutes later to put Bayern in the box seat. Olise scored on 73 minutes and Kane converted a penalty with four minutes remaining to seal victory.

On Tuesday, Borussia Dortmund beat fifth-division amateur side HEBC 5-0 in Hamburg.

articles.title: Birds stop play but Medvedev flies into third round
articles.summary: An interruption from a pair of birds ruffles Daniil Medvedev's feathers but fails to disrupt the seventh seed as he eases into the US Open third round with a...
articles.body:
An interruption from a pair of birds ruffled Daniil Medvedev's feathers but could not disrupt the seventh seed as he eased into the US Open third round with a dominant victory over Sebastian Gorzny.

The two birds settled down on the net for a closer look at the action midway through a second-set rally, with play continuing around them for several strokes before the chair umpire called for the point to be replayed.

Medvedev, who placed the incident in his "top five" most unusual experiences at the New York major, was visibly stunned by the decision which came just after he thought he had won the point with a cross-court forehand.

"This is very bad," the 2021 champion said as he remonstrated at the umpire on court.

Medvedev is no stranger to losing his composure on court, notably receiving a fine of almost £31,500 at last year's US Open for an extraordinary meltdown during his first-round defeat to Benjamin Bonzi.

As recently as last month's Winston-Salem Open, where he again lost in the opening round, he spent a disconsolate change of ends questioning his future in the sport, musing "maybe I should start a career in pickleball".

However, the 30-year-old, who had already flown through the first set in just 21 minutes, quickly brushed aside the avian interruption to complete a straightforward 6-1 6-3 7-5 win over American wildcard Gorzny, the world number 731.

"I saw [the birds] straight away," Medvedev said in his on-court interview. "I thought the point would stop straight away but it didn't.

"Then we play for 45 seconds and the moment I hit the winner we say stop. I'm like, 'Why? We played for 45 seconds!'.

"But it's okay. I was not happy with the decision but it is was it is. You can't do anything with it.

"The situation was pretty crazy but I love this court, I'm happy to win, to stay in the US Open, to stay in New York for longer."

The Russian will play Frenchman Arthur Rinderknech in the third round.

images.caption: Medvedev has only advanced to the second week of a major once in seven tournaments since reaching the US Open quarter-finals in 2024 [Getty Images]

articles.title: Arrest made in break-in at home of Eagles RB Saquon Barkley
articles.summary: An arrest has been made in connection with the attempted burglary at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.
articles.body:
An arrest has been made in connection with the attempted burglary at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.

The Montgomery County District Attorney's Office announced Wednesday that 24-year-old Jabir Parker of Philadelphia has been arrested in connection with the crime.

Parker faces multiple felony charges, including burglary, conspiracy to burglarize, criminal trespass (breaking into a structure) and other related offenses.

Authorities allege Parker broke into Barkley's home in Tredyffrin Township, Chester County, during the early morning hours of July 18.

According to investigators, Barkley and his family were inside the home at the time of the burglary, but no one was injured.

Suspects sought in burglary at Saquon Barkley's Malvern home

Prosecutors said Parker is also accused of stealing nearly $1 million worth of jewelry during burglaries at two homes in Montgomery County.

Detectives used cellphone location data, commonly known as geofencing, to link Parker's phone to the crime scenes, according to authorities.

Stay with Action News as we continue to follow this developing story.
